Degradation products and pathways: Hot-water ageing of a commercial mineral-wool PUF binder releases soluble phenol/urea/formaldehyde-derived fragments. Ether-like bridges are more hydrolysis-sensitive than methylene bridges; mass spectra also indicate cleavage of urea units to amino-terminated fragments. Cure history changes resistance.

Environmental persistence: Moisture can detach binder from mineral fibers and release soluble organic fragments. The study provides no transferable lifetime in soil, freshwater, seawater or landfill.
